_comment_case: Realistic E. coli swimming case: one left-handed helical filament at the tail
pole, driven by a rotary motor (free_torsion root + constant stall torque with
linear speed limit).  The cell swims in +X with the flagellum trailing behind.
Regenerate the CSV files with geometry/generate_ecoli_geometry.m.

custom_geometry._comment_body: Sphero-cylinder 2.5 um long x 0.88 um diameter (Berg 2004); N_body = 300 requested, laid out by capsule_body_building (326 points actually generated).

pili._comment: Flagellar filament: left-handed helix, pitch 2.22 um, diameter 0.41 um, ~7.6 um contour (Turner et al. 2000).

motor_torque._comment: Stall torque ~1300 pN nm, zero-load speed ~300 Hz (Berg 2003; Chen & Berg 2000); linear torque-speed curve.

_comment_material: Filament radius 10 nm (20 nm diameter).  E is chosen so that the bending
stiffness EI = E*pi*r^4/4 = 3.5e-24 N m^2 (3.5 pN um^2; Darnton & Berg 2007).
sigma_p = 0.2 gives GJ = EI/(1+sigma) ~ 2.9e-24 N m^2, within the measured range.
_comment_fluid: Water at ~20 C.  rho_bac = rho_fluid (neutrally buoyant cell): gravity / sedimentation is switched off.

_comment_cost: The filament turns at ~150 Hz, so ode15s needs ~70 internal steps per rotation.
Reference cost (this PC, earlier 205-point body, seg_per_um = 5): ~29 min of wall
time for 0.2 s of simulated time.  T_obs = 1 s with the 326-point body is not yet
timed; expect several hours (roughly 5x the simulated time and a larger system).
simulation._comment_dt: dt sets only the output sampling stride (1 ms = ~7 frames per filament rotation); ode15s adapts its internal step.
